meta.title: SSC Stenographer Grade C & D - 30 Minute Mock Test
instructions: The examination consists of Objective Type, Multiple choice questions.
The total duration for this practice test is 30 minutes.
There will be a negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer.
No marks will be deducted for unattempted questions.
The English Language and Comprehension section must be attempted in English only.
Candidates are not permitted to use calculators or any other electronic devices.

questions.text: Look at this series: 7, 10, 8, 11, 9, 12, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is a simple alternating addition and subtraction series. The pattern is +3, -2, +3, -2, and so on. (7+3=10; 10-2=8; 8+3=11; 11-2=9; 9+3=12). The next step is 12-2=10.

questions.text: Select the related word pair from the given alternatives: Book : Publisher :: Film : ?
questions.explanation: Just as a 'Publisher' is responsible for financing and producing a 'Book', a 'Producer' is responsible for financing and producing a 'Film'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'DOG' is written as 'EPH'. How is 'CAT' written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter in the word is shifted forward by one place in the alphabetical order. D(+1)=E, O(+1)=P, G(+1)=H. Similarly, C(+1)=D, A(+1)=B, T(+1)=U. So, CAT becomes DBU.

questions.text: Pointing to a woman, Abhijit said, 'Her granddaughter is the only daughter of my brother.' How is the woman related to Abhijit?
questions.explanation: Abhijit's brother's only daughter is Abhijit's niece. The woman's granddaughter is this niece. Therefore, the woman must be the mother of Abhijit and his brother.

questions.text:
Statements: All cars are cats. All fans are cats. 
Conclusions: I. All cars are fans. II. Some fans are cars.
options: D) Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Cars and fans are both subsets of cats, but there is no direct relationship established between cars and fans in the statements. Therefore, neither conclusion logically follows.

questions.text: Article 32 of the Indian Constitution deals with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, which means a person has the right to move to the Supreme Court for getting their fundamental rights protected. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

questions.text: Who among the following was affectionately known as the 'Frontier Gandhi'?
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a Pashtun independence activist and was commonly known as Frontier Gandhi because of his close association with Mahatma Gandhi and his adherence to non-violence.

questions.text: Which of the following is the longest river in Peninsular India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari is the largest and longest river in Peninsular India. It is also known as the Dakshin Ganga (Ganges of the South).

questions.text: What is the chemical name of Vitamin C?
questions.explanation: The chemical name of Vitamin C is Ascorbic Acid. Its deficiency causes scurvy. Retinol is Vitamin A, Calciferol is Vitamin D, and Thiamine is Vitamin B1.

questions.text: The famous 'Hornbill Festival' is celebrated in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill Festival is a major annual cultural festival organized by the State Tourism and Art & Culture Departments of Nagaland, showcasing the state's rich traditions.

questions.text: Choose the correct synonym of the given word: OBSOLETE
questions.explanation: Obsolete means no longer produced or used; out of date. Therefore, 'Outdated' is the closest synonym.

questions.text: Choose the correct antonym of the given word: TRANSPARENT
questions.explanation: Transparent means allowing light to pass through so that objects behind can be distinctly seen. 'Opaque' means not able to be seen through; not transparent.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: 'A piece of cake'
questions.explanation: The idiom 'A piece of cake' is used to describe a task that can be accomplished very easily.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: 'Bite the bullet'
options: A) To get into a physical fight
B) To face a difficult or unpleasant situation bravely
C) To eat something very hard
D) To run away from danger
questions.explanation: 'To bite the bullet' means to endure a painful or otherwise unpleasant situation that is seen as unavoidable.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error: 'Neither of the two sisters are going to the party.'
questions.explanation: The error lies in 'are going'. 'Neither of' is followed by a plural noun/pronoun but takes a singular verb. It should be 'is going'.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error: 'He is one of the best student in his class.'
questions.explanation: The phrase 'one of the' must always be followed by a plural noun. So, it should be 'students' instead of 'student'.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word: 'She has been living in this city ___ 2015.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used for a point in time (a specific year, day, time, etc.), whereas 'for' is used for a period or duration of time. Since 2015 is a specific point, 'since' is correct.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition: 'I am not very good ___ mathematics.'
questions.explanation: The correct preposition to use after the adjective 'good' to indicate proficiency in a subject or activity is 'at' (e.g., good at sports, good at math).

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence: 'The mechanic repaired my car.'
options: A) My car is repaired by the mechanic.
B) My car was repaired by the mechanic.
C) My car has been repaired by the mechanic.
D) My car is being repaired by the mechanic.
questions.explanation: The active sentence is in simple past tense (repaired). The passive format for simple past is 'was/were + V3'. Thus, 'was repaired' is correct.

questions.text: Select the correct active form of the given sentence: 'Let the door be closed.'
questions.explanation: The given passive sentence is an imperative command. The active form of 'Let + object + be + V3' is an imperative starting with V1 + object (Close the door).

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence: He said, 'I have passed the examination.'
options: A) He said that he had passed the examination.
B) He said that he has passed the examination.
C) He said that I had passed the examination.
D) He told that he passed the examination.
questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said' is in past tense. So, present perfect (have passed) changes to past perfect (had passed) in indirect speech. The pronoun 'I' changes to 'he'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence: The teacher said to the students, 'The earth revolves around the sun.'
options: A) The teacher told the students that the earth revolved around the sun.
B) The teacher asked the students if the earth revolves around the sun.
C) The teacher told the students that the earth revolves around the sun.
D) The teacher said to the students the earth revolve around the sun.
questions.explanation: When the reported speech states a universal truth or a scientific fact, the tense remains unchanged. 'Said to' changes to 'told'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment: 'He is the best of the two boys.'
options: B) most best of the two
questions.explanation: When comparing two things or people, the comparative degree must be used, not the superlative degree. Therefore, 'better' is correct instead of 'best'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given: 'A person who cannot read or write'
questions.explanation: 'Illiterate' specifically refers to someone unable to read or write. 'Uneducated' is broader and means poorly educated, while 'Ignorant' means lacking knowledge.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Accommodation', which requires double 'c' and double 'm'.
